title: Extension of a supplied finite closed free local map
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], i:Z -> X a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], F a coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], r a natural number, U an open of X, and phi:(i_*(O_Z^{direct sum r}))|U -> F|U a given map. There is a coherent ideal I on Z [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] such that the natural inclusion j:i_*(I^{direct sum r}) -> i_*(O_Z^{direct sum r}) is invertible on U, and there is a global map alpha:i_*(I^{direct sum r}) -> F satisfying alpha|U = (j|U) followed by phi. Z need not be integral, U may be empty, and phi need not be injective or invertible.

source.place: Tag 01YB extension clause, used on a finite closed free source as in Tag 01YE, last paragraph; affine closed-pushforward calculation of Tag 01QY.

proof.text: Construct the finite closed free source. Reindex the free generators by ULift(Fin r), produce finite locally free generator data, and transport back. Finite pushforward preserves quasi-coherence and finite type; the locally Noetherian coherence criterion makes the source coherent and the target quasi-coherent.

Construct K as the vanishing ideal of X minus U. The proved support formula identifies its support. Tensor extension produces n and beta, and the image-lifting lemma produces m and a, with a followed by tensor multiplication equal to the inclusion of K^(n+m)H.

Set I=(K^(n+m)).comap i. The source scheme is locally Noetherian. Its ideal module is the kernel of the structure-to-closed-pushforward map; the closed pushforward is quasi-coherent, so the proved Noetherian kernel theorem makes I finitely presented and hence coherent. Apply the normalized finite closed free product comparison.

The support of K^(n+m) is contained in that of K, so its inclusion is invertible on U by the proved ideal restriction lemma. Monoidality makes tensor multiplication invertible on U. Its image inclusion is epi from the image factorization, and mono because restriction preserves limits, thus invertible. Transport through the comparison to obtain the desired lattice inclusion. Set alpha=e.hom followed by a followed by beta; functoriality, associativity and the two normalization equations prove its required restriction equality.

theorem coherent_local_free_ideal_lattice
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F)
    (r : ℕ) (U : X.Opens)
    (φ : (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj
        ((pushforward i).obj (∐ fun _ : Fin r => SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)) ⟶
      (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj F) :
    ∃ (I : Z.IdealSheafData),
      RingedSpace.IsCoherent Z.toRingedSpace I.toModules ∧
      IsIso ((restrictFunctor U.ι).map
        ((pushforward i).map (Sigma.desc (fun j : Fin r ↦ I.toModulesι ≫
          Sigma.ι (fun _ : Fin r ↦ SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf) j)))) ∧
      ∃ (α : (pushforward i).obj (∐ fun _ : Fin r => I.toModules) ⟶ F),
        (restrictFunctor U.ι).map α =
          (restrictFunctor U.ι).map
            ((pushforward i).map (Sigma.desc (fun j : Fin r ↦ I.toModulesι ≫
          Sigma.ι (fun _ : Fin r ↦ SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf) j))) ≫ φ
